speed.head: ⏩ Speed
speed.warnTooShort: Cannot set {s}× — the clip would be shorter than {min}s. Trim a longer source segment first.
speed.warnOverlap: Not enough room on the timeline — the clip would be {dur} long and overlap the next clip. Move the other clip first.
speed.warnResetOverlap: Not enough room to reset to 1× — move the other clip first.
speed.tip: 💡 Speed changes tempo but keeps voice pitch. Reverse plays from the end of the source back to the start.
speed.curveTip: 💡 A speed curve creates real speed keyframes: preview and render both follow the curve. While enabled, the constant speed above is overridden by the curve.
speed.curveNote: Curve enabled — the constant speed above is overridden by the curve; preview follows the curve and render splits segments along the curve.
speed.warnReverseRamp: ⚠️ Clip is reversed — reverse CANNOT be combined with speedKeyframes, render will be blocked. Turn off reverse or the speed curve.
speed.warnStabilizeRamp: ⚠️ Clip has both stabilization and a speed curve — the validator blocks this combination, render will be blocked. Turn off one of them.
speed.warnNoGap: No gap ≥ 0.2s left to add a point — move points apart first.
speed.bezierHead: Bezier factors (cubic-bezier: x1, y1, x2, y2):
speed.bezierHint: x1, x2 must be within [0, 1]; y1, y2 are free (outside [0, 1] creates overshoot).
speed.bezierXRange: Bezier x1, x2 must be within [0, 1] — previous value kept.
speed.bezierInvalid: Bezier values must be numbers — previous value kept.
speed.trimCurveDropped: ✂️ Trimmed {n} speed-curve point(s) that fell outside the clip — remaining points kept. Use Undo to restore them if you did not intend this.
speed.patchCurveDropped: ✂️ Trimmed {n} speed-curve point(s) that fell outside the clip after the duration change — remaining points kept. Use Undo to restore them if you did not intend this.

motion.tipSelect: Select a video clip on the timeline to adjust slow-mo / frame interpolation / motion blur.
motion.tipUnsupported: Slow-mo / frame interpolation is for video clips only ({kind} is not supported yet).
motion.intro: Frame interpolation creates in-between frames for smoother slow motion; motion blur blends several frames to create motion streaks.
motion.warnRenderOnly: Slow-mo / interpolation / motion blur only take effect on render — the preview is only approximate, not the real render result.
motion.targetFpsNote: Target fps only applies when interpolation is on.
motion.miModeNote: Interpolation mode only applies when interpolation is on.
motion.warnLong: A long clip + interpolation renders slowly — try a short segment first before rendering the whole clip.
motion.warnStabilize: ⚠️ This clip has both stabilization and a speed curve — the validator blocks this combination, so the render will be blocked. Interpolation + stabilization (without a speed curve) can be combined.
motion.warnTransitionFps: ⚠️ Target fps ({target}) differs from project fps ({project}) and this clip has a transition — xfade requires both inputs at the same fps, so the render will be blocked (fail-fast). Set target fps back to project fps or remove the transition.
motion.warnFpsMismatch: Target fps ({target}) differs from project fps ({project}) but this clip has no transition, so the render still runs — the final output is resampled back to project fps, so only part of the smoothness remains.
motion.costEstimate: Estimate (not a measured figure): clip {dur}s × {fps} fps ≈ {frames} output frames ({ratio}× project fps). Real render time depends on hardware/codec and has not been measured — this only gauges workload, it is not a time commitment.
motion.blurWeightsLabel: Per-frame weights (always normalized to a total of 1):
motion.blurWeightsNote: Per-frame weights are set with sliders (1–100%); the total is always normalized to 1. Changing the frame count resets to an even split and discards custom weights.
motion.disableAll: Turn off all slow-mo / motion blur

nested.title: 📦 Nested clip (compound clip)
nested.note: Nest several clips into a single clip on the timeline.
nested.needTwo: Select at least 2 clips on the timeline to nest.
nested.missingClip: A selected clip no longer exists.
nested.nestedOrLayer: Cannot nest a nested clip or adjustment layer.
nested.nestOk: Nested into a compound clip (1 undo step).
nested.nestFail: Could not nest — check the selection (see the reason above).
nested.unnestOk: Unnested back to the original clips (1 undo step).
nested.unnestFail: Could not unnest — restored clips may overlap other clips.
nested.innerCurveDropped: Warning: {n} speed keyframe(s) outside the new duration were dropped from the curve — use Undo to restore them if you did not intend this.
nested.innerSaveFail: Could not save the inner clip — check for overlaps or exceeding the compound clip.
nested.speedRejected: Nested clip “{name}” carries {fields}, so splitting/trimming it is rejected: a valid speed ramp can still be split/trimmed — the render worker forbids only {reason}. {fix}
nested.speedRejectedFixBoth: Remove the speed curve and turn off reverse on the nested clip, then try again.
nested.speedRejectedFixReverse: Turn off reverse on the nested clip, then try again.
nested.speedRejectedFixCurve: Remove the speed curve from the nested clip, then try again.
nested.speedRejectedReasonReverse: reverse (reversing the inner timeline is not supported)
nested.speedRejectedReasonCurve: an invalid curve (empty, malformed, with an uncomputable integral, a mismatched trim window, or a speed outside [0.25, 4])
nested.speedRejectedReasonCurveEmpty: an empty curve (no curve to map through)
nested.speedRejectedReasonCurveShape: a malformed curve (an invalid keyframe, or more than 128 keyframes)
nested.speedRejectedReasonCurveIntegral: a curve whose integral cannot be computed
nested.speedRejectedReasonCurveWindow: a trim window mismatched with the curve integral
nested.fixedTrimNotNested: This clip is not a nested clip.
nested.fixedTrimTwoLevel: A clip inside the nested clip already carries a speed curve — merging two curve levels is not supported yet (spec round 18 §5).
nested.fixedTrimUncomputable: Cannot compute the duration in keep-trim mode (invalid curve/trim, nested clip is reversed, or the computed duration is under 0.2s).
nested.curveTwoLevel: Cannot set a speed curve on nested clip “{name}”: a clip inside already carries a speed curve — merging two curve levels is not supported yet (spec round 18 §5). Remove the inner clip's curve and try again.
nested.curveTwoLevelInvalid: Cannot create two curve levels on nested clip “{name}”: {reason}
nested.curveIntegralMismatch: Nested clip “{name}” will be rejected by render: trim.out ({actualOut}) differs from in + speed-curve integral ({expectedOut}) by more than 1e-4s. Fix the trim or the curve so they match, then try again.
nested.curveOverSource: Warning: the speed curve of nested clip “{name}” consumes up to {expectedOut}s of the inner source, exceeding the inner source duration {sourceDuration}s — the tail may have no picture.
nested.curveModeFixedDuration: Keep duration, recompute trim.out from the integral
nested.curveModeNote: Keep-duration is the default behaviour when setting a curve; keep-trim changes the clip length on the timeline.
nested.curveModePreviewDuration: Applying with this mode: keep duration {dur}s → new trim.out {out}s
nested.curveModePreviewTrim: Applying with this mode: keep trim [{tin}, {tout}) → new duration {dur}s
nested.curveModePreviewFail: Cannot compute the expected value for the current curve (invalid curve/trim, nested clip is reversed, or the computed duration is under 0.2s).
nested.curveModeApply: Apply curve with the selected mode
nested.curveModeApplyOk: Speed curve applied with the selected mode (1 undo step).
nested.curveModeAlreadyOk: The curve already matches the selected mode — nothing to re-apply.
nested.curveModeApplyFail: Could not apply the speed curve with the selected mode — see the reason above.
nested.curveCreateNote: Starting preset: constant 1× speed (1 keyframe) — safe: its integral equals the duration, so the merged speed never exceeds [0.25, 4]. After creating, edit the curve with the mode block below.
nested.curveCreatePreviewChange: After creating (keeping duration {dur}s): trim.out {oldOut}s → {newOut}s (from the constant-1× curve integral)
nested.curveCreatePreviewFail: Cannot compute the expected trim.out for the starting curve (invalid trim/duration) — no curve created.
nested.curveCreateOk: Speed curve created (constant 1×) — 1 undo step to remove it.
nested.curveCreateAlreadyHas: This nested clip already has a speed curve — use the mode block below to edit it.
nested.curveCreateReverse: Cannot create a speed curve on a reversed nested clip (the validator forbids reverse + curve — turn off reverse and try again).
nested.curveCreateFail: Could not create the speed curve — the clip may have been deleted or the store refused; nothing changed.

adjustment.title: 🎛 Adjustment layer
adjustment.note: An effect layer applied to every clip below it within its time range. Layers live on the separate FX row above the video tracks.
adjustment.noVideoTrack: Need at least 1 video track to hold an adjustment layer.
adjustment.addFail: Could not add — check: need a video track, duration >= 0.2s, no overlapping layer.
adjustment.saveFail: Could not save the layer — check for overlapping layers.
adjustment.specNote: Standard layers are written to spec.adjustmentLayers (project level): they apply to every video clip overlapping in time, and layers may overlap (filters chain in order). Old layers still show separately below with a legacy badge.
adjustment.scopeSingleBlocked: One-track scope cannot be created yet: video-spec has no scope field for adjustment layers, so the panel will not write a fake scope into the spec. Pick “All tracks” to create the layer, or wait for the spec thread to add a scope field (see R7_UI_LIMITS.md).
adjustment.specAddFail: Could not add the standard layer — check the filter, intensity 0..1, duration >= 0.2s.
adjustment.convertOk: Legacy layer converted to the standard spec (1 undo step).
adjustment.convertFail: Could not convert — this legacy layer has an invalid filter.
adjustment.complexFilter: Complex layer (LUT/color/multiple effects) — the panel can only edit its timing.
adjustment.specSaveFail: Could not save the standard layer — check timing and filter.
adjustment.trackSelectAria: Track to apply to when one track is selected

nestedBoundary.title: Transition across boundary + opacity
nestedBoundary.note: Only the fade type is joined across a nested boundary (R3): other types are rejected, nothing is written. Each end needs an adjacent clip touching the boundary exactly (no gap); do not set both an in and an out transition. Opacity 0..1 multiplies into each leaf clip.
nestedBoundary.saveOk: Transition/opacity saved for the nested clip (1 undo step).
nestedBoundary.saveFail: Could not save — check: fade only, adjacent clips touching the boundary, not both ends, opacity 0..1.
